        "All 470 owned diff lines across all 8 eligible paths were read, including the new browser test, XML autoconfig fixture and header file, OAuth unit test, manifest registration and test-provider scope change. Metadata and positive/negative product-directive preflight found no excluded product body in this cohort. The fixture uses mock plain IMAP/SMTP endpoints; it is not a production transport recommendation.",
        "The new click branch accepts a matching composed target, initializes OAuth with a null username using a hostname preference, waits for the listener token and base64url-decodes its payload. It forwards preferred_username and name-or-username into the existing autoConfigSubview flow. It does not skip all setup steps. The original guard only checks the matching button; the fixed accepted branch additionally checks current state and disabled state. Local token decoding does not itself establish JWT signature, issuer, audience or expiry verification.",
        "The new AbortController calls cancelPrompt and clears the loading state. The actual back-event branch cancels an active operation and stays in its current subview; reset also aborts active work. The setter exposes Cancel through the footer. cancelPrompt calls the inner authorization-failure and finish methods. These scoped calls support cancellation wiring, not a claim that closing an external browser tab completes authentication or that every outer lifecycle path was exercised.",
        "Only a refresh-token or scope change enters the new username-learning block. A strictly null username and one of the two Thundermail origins or external.test is required. The payload preferred_username is assigned to both wrapper and inner OAuth objects before setRefreshToken. Initialization searches reusable objects by endpoint, username and scope superset; the unit test directly checks reuse for the learned username and non-reuse for another null username. No claim is made for arbitrary providers, malformed claims or token cryptographic validity.",
        "The new JSON/base64url decode runs inside an async success callback passed to connect().then(success, failure). That callback does not return or catch the resulting promise. Its sibling failure callback covers rejection of connect, not a throw or rejection from the success callback. The Account Hub waits for listener callbacks. The inspected accepted code retains this local gap; it is not a reproduced hang or proof that all external cleanup is absent.",
        "The browser test directly checks saved login fields and incoming/outgoing configuration after mock OAuth and autoconfig. Twelve original account/server assertions omit a message; short login-field labels are nonempty but do not state the expected value. The original test does not directly assert name/fallback prefill. The accepted test adds three identity assertions in a later phase, also without messages. Its new unit test instead gives nonempty result messages and forces both URL-safe characters. No missing-should-only defect is reported.",
        "The unit test covers learned username, saved login origin/username/refresh token and inner-object identity. Both test tokens are fabricated foo.payload.baz values, so these assertions establish test intent and claim plumbing, not signature verification, real account creation, external browser behavior or a live provider response. No malformed-token, abort or name-fallback case is added. The browser setup calls pushPrefEnv without awaiting it; no fresh harness timing result is inferred.",
        "The source uses early guards, separate setup/action/assertion groups and concrete callback receiver choices. The getAccessToken API is callback-based here; the new Account Hub wraps it in Promise.withResolvers. initFromHostname returns a Boolean, but the new caller does not inspect it. Required production provider configuration, native/browser prompt implementations and linked ChromeUtils/ExchangeAutoDiscover bodies remain bounded context rather than new global conventions.",

Source instead forwards the decoded values into the existing autoConfigSubview flow.",

The author rejects the proposed deepEqual explanation: only selected fields matter, rather than an asserted XPCOM limitation. This is a scoped test choice, not a general ban on structural assertions.",

Its original 12 account/server assertions have no messages; its unit test directly checks URL-safe characters, learned identity, persisted token and reuse. Review approval and reported remote completion do not fill malformed-token, cancellation, real-name fallback or real-provider coverage. The external-page close failure is the reviewer historical experiment, not our execution."

        "All 10 owned paths and all 1,347 diff lines are read, including the extraction, code generation, tests, supported-path list and complete generated move operation. The initial long output was truncated; the missing middle was read in bounded file sections before source completion.",
        "The patch passes SchemaContext through body extraction, distinguishes request/specific success/other schemas, and renames operation.delta to is_delta. Only a non-delta object with properties in a request or response context becomes an unnamed object. Nested objects remain explicitly unsupported. anyOf retains supported references, warns for other alternatives, and still reaches ApiBody's single-property assertion rather than implementing arbitrary union bodies.",
        "Unnamed properties produce method-specific PostRequestBody or ResponseBody names and carry a GraphType. The emitter places those definitions alongside path operations, omits named-type selection/module documentation, and suppresses generated accessor docs for unnamed types under an explicitly linked rustc diagnostic workaround. That upstream issue body is unread; the workaround is local source, not a Rust-wide comment rule.",
        "The historical request_with_body code uses an if/else-if, so it collects an unnamed request type or an unnamed response type, not both together. The selected accepted emitter retains the same at-most-one choice with UnnamedObjectSchema. No simultaneous anonymous-request-and-response case is covered or claimed supported.",
        "The new generated move module exports a PostRequestBody backed by PropertyMap and a DestinationId getter/setter, constructs POST with a Message response, and serializes OperationBody::JSON. The accepted generated module has moved into a nested path and later uses a plain optional destination_id field with PascalCase serde naming and selectable responses. The actual Graph caller constructs that current field and passes JSON; later representation/query changes are not part of this original generator landing.",
        "The new extraction tests assert one top-level unnamed type, its PostRequestBody name, two properties, string/i32 field types, and exclusions for delta/Other contexts. Property checks use find by name on the HashMap-derived vector. The negative cases only assert that no returned property is unnamed; they do not assert a complete expected output schema. No tests for nested objects or anonymous request plus anonymous response are added.",
        "The changed media-resource assert! in extract/path.rs has no assertion message; it replaces an already message-less assert_eq! and still needs a non-empty expected-behavior diagnostic. The new unnamed-object assertions do have meaningful messages with should. The later accepted navigation-property assertions are outside this original change.",
        "Manual checks keep the local Rust enum/context names, explicit limitations and separated import/property-generation steps. Full D293132 later requests tests, is_delta naming, a specific-response comment and a logging rebase; actual source adopts these. Its reported NumberProp/StringProp intermittent is resolved in source by name lookup, not an imposed map order. Historical rustfmt failures, remote completion and approval are not fresh checks.",
        "Source A read complete primary Bug 2030283 once during the current collector; reuse original 94e39cd222d911a1a4b199cd19193c01a35cfbee172ce4cb0601d548f3795cf8 with original time/scope. No separate API-spec body or generated-output run was opened.",
        "Source C collected full D293132 and Source A read its retained creation-to-final timeline and all six submitted inline bodies. Requests for tests, direct is_delta naming, a specific-response explanation and rebase after logging moved to D291313 are adopted in the actual owned source. Done markers alone are not adoption proof.",
        "The reviewer reports an intermittent that expected StringProp first but received NumberProp.
